settings.heading: It started with grandma's tin.
settings.content: No lab. No focus groups. Just a farmhouse kitchen, a slow cooker, and a stubborn belief that skincare got needlessly complicated.

settings.title: The tin by the sink
settings.text: Grandma kept rendered tallow by the kitchen sink — for chapped hands, wind-burned cheeks, scraped knees.

settings.title: 47 messy batches
settings.text: Staring at a shelf of $60 creams we couldn't pronounce, we went back to her recipe and whipped it 47 times.

settings.title: The first 100 jars
settings.text: We hand-filled a hundred jars at the kitchen table and gave them to friends. They came back for more.

settings.title: 8,200 happy faces
settings.text: Same four ingredients. Same small batches. Just a lot more sinks with a jar beside them.
We'll never put a fifth ingredient in just to sound fancy.
We'll never make a claim our own skin can't back up.
